title: PERCEPTION DETERMINES REALITY
subtitle: Anti-Rollback Authority Fencing and Stale-Snapshot Recovery Extension
problem_statement: A valid historical snapshot can be cryptographically authentic and still be causally stale. Restoring it without an external authority fence can resurrect old credentials, old obligations and old assumptions while ignoring world effects that occurred later.

new_primitives.AUTHORITY_EPOCH_ID: Monotonic authority generation for one host commit channel.
new_primitives.FENCE_TOKEN: Monotonic or otherwise non-reusable authority value recognized by the external effect boundary.
new_primitives.MINIMUM_ACCEPTED_AUTHORITY_EPOCH: Lowest current authority generation accepted for world-changing commits.
new_primitives.STALE_SNAPSHOT_STATUS: Classification for a valid old state that does not hold current authority.
new_primitives.ROLLBACK_RECOVERY_EVENT: Explicit event that reopens an old checkpoint without pretending later history never occurred.

required: FENCE_TOKEN or equivalent freshness condition passes
commit sequence is not below current protected floor

rollback_recovery_algorithm: select historical checkpoint with exact provenance
preserve the newer suffix as historical/forensic evidence
restore old state in a non-authoritative recovery context
replay later externally evidenced obligations and world effects
issue a fresh authority epoch and fence token
emit a recovery checkpoint linking old checkpoint and later suffix

examples: fulfilled obligation remains fulfilled if an external receipt survives
promise already communicated to a Free Other remains historical fact
harm or repair already caused is not removed by loading an old save

implementation_tests: authentic old snapshot with stale authority epoch cannot commit
historical signature verifies but current fence rejects
fulfilled obligation in external receipt is not performed twice after rollback
rollback without explicit recovery event fails
recovery event preserves newer suffix reference
fresh authority epoch is required before restored state becomes current
epistemic_boundaries: An old snapshot is not necessarily false or corrupted; it is stale relative to later causal history.
Fencing requires an external or monotonic boundary that stale state cannot silently reset.
Rollback control is a systems-integrity mechanism, not a claim about personal consciousness or resurrection.
canonical_lines: Valid then is not authoritative now.
Loading an old memory does not unload the world.
Rollback must create a recovery event, not erase the suffix.
